pr_title: enhancement!: use server.globalProxy value for creating a global http/https proxy
pr_body:
### What does it do?

- Move `server.proxy` to `server.proxy.koa`
- Move `server.globalProxy` to `server.proxy.global`
- add `server.proxy.fetch` to act only on Fetch requests  (defaults to proxy.global if set)
- add `server.proxy.http` to act on `http` requests (defaults to proxy.global if set)
- add `server.proxy.https` to act on `https` requests (defaults to proxy.global if set)

This

### Why is it needed?

Allows proxy of all http and https requests globally (including anything that uses http/https internally, such as axios, passport-oauth2, etc, giving Strapi an actual global proxy to solve issues like [proxied SSO](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/17317)

### How to test it?

- set server.proxy.global (or ad individual value) in your config
- use something like `npx http-echo-server` to create an echo proxy
- set up SSO (or whatever feature you want to test proxied)
- when you use SSO, you should see it proxied through your echo server
- fetch requests (such as telemetry) should still come through to the echo proxy

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

Fixes https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/17317

DX-989

Documentation PR: https://github.com/strapi/documentation/pull/2124

TODO:

- [ ] write a codemod to migrate server.proxy -> server.proxy.koa and server.globalProxy -> server.proxy.global which will come in a later PR

issue_context.title: Passport SSO providers do not use the globalProxy when fetching user information
issue_context.body:
## Bug report

### Required System information

- Node.js version: 18
- NPM version: 8
- Strapi version: 4.11.5
- Database: SQLite
- Operating system: Linux Mint 21.1
- Is your project Javascript or Typescript: Javascript

### Describe the bug

All of the passport.js providers we recommend in our documentation are not getting the proxy agent constructed from the `globalProxy` config option as we don't pass in the `strapi.fetch.agent` but even if we did/could it appears that a nested package `passport-oauth2` doesn't even have a mechanism for passing in an http proxy agent anyway.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Setup for testing is quite complex as you will need to install something like squid and configure it in your Strapi application. However if you want to take a look at a sample repo I constructed as a workaround for a customer and work backwards from there you can see how I got around it.

https://github.com/strapi-support-demo-apps/strapi-example-v4-sso-proxy

### Expected behavior

Honestly I don't know what we can do if the downstream libs don't support passing in a proxy other than going with a forced global proxy to force all traffic over the proxy however this will break implementations where a user only wants some traffic to go over the proxy and not custom http calls that say need access to resources on the local machine or in the same internal network.

### Screenshots

see example repo

### Code snippets

see example repo

### Additional context

Related to internal TID 4233
comments: Patch given to the EE customer was this one to override the nested provider to support proxies: https://github.com/strapi-support-demo-apps/strapi-example-v4-sso-proxy
